# Why Microsoft Azure Functions

It's a major growing  world cloud provider, its growing in my region (south east asia) and I had good learning experience with Microsoft in the past. 

### Growing cloud usage

Microsoft was my choice because it's a top 3 cloud provider in the world, 2nd in ranking and increasing its market share the last 5 years [(source)](https://www.
srgresearch.com/articles/cloud-market-share-trends-big-three-together-hold-63-while-oracle-and-the-neoclouds-inch-higher). In 2026 it's remains at this position holding 21% of the global market [(source)](https://www.statista.com/chart/18819/worldwide-market-share-of-leading-cloud-infrastructure-service-providers/).

### Growing region presence

I'm currently located in Thailand where Microsoft is present and active [(source)](https://news.microsoft.com/apac/2024/05/01/microsoft-announces-significant-commitments-to-enable-a-cloud-and-ai-powered-future-for-thailand/). It's expanding its infrastructure in the country with a data center coming up in Bangkok by 2028 [(source)](https://www.thailandnow.in.th/business-investment/microsoft-announces-1b-thailand-investment-amid-ai-hub-ambitions/). As of May 2026 the Azure region "Thailand South" is not yet available [(source)](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/explore/global-infrastructure/regions/?tabs=azure-portal&expanded=azure-portal-expanded).

### Azure Fabric and Functions

Some time ago I passed the Azure Fabric Data Engineer certification [(source)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/users/alexandrecagnon-1774/) to get my hands dirty on top of the shelf products from a major cloud provider. I very much liked exploring Fabric because it was challenging: so many IaaS to SaaS products to wisely choose from, numerous tricky configurations, so many ways to spin up a Spark cluster, so many governance rules to available... Fabric is undoubtedly a powerful platform - data engineering at least based on my experience.

One thing that I missed in this certificate was demonstrations to run code with lightweight engines. Using Fabric for data engineering is like welding a huge hammer. It's powerfull but not appropriate for every nail. In Fabric, Spark is the pivotal tool of the Azure Fabric plateform and my feeling is that it adds significant costs that are not justified for small to medium sized projects. That's a big data processing plateform, not a got to solution for any data engineering and analytics project. Before hammering with Fabric, you better have good reasons to do so and be ready for serious setup and maintenance costs.

### Azure Functions

For some data analytics project I was looking for a lightweight cost efficient data processing solution (low CPU, MEM, Disk, Network, etc.) that could scale from few requests to thousands a day. Azure Functions looked like the perfect solution: a serverless compute service that allows to run Python code on Azure at a cheap transparent cost. There's even a free tier to get started and scale up as needed [(source)](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/functions/).

The question was then to start developing and testing Azure Functions locally before deploying to Azure. That's the subject of this blog post.


# Setup local development environment

## Install Azure Functions Core Tools

1. Create a new directory on your laptop to host the Azure Functions project
```dosbat
mkdir C:\Users\alexa\Documents\PRO_PROJECTS\demo_projects\azure_function_local
cd C:\Users\alexa\Documents\PRO_PROJECTS\demo_projects\azure_function_local
```

## An Azure Functions within minutes

You can do it manually or [(install Azure Functions Core Tools)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/functions-run-local?tabs=windows%2Cisolated-process%2Cnode-v4%2Cpython-v2%2Chttp-trigger%2Ccontainer-apps&pivots=programming-language-python) to take advantage of the CLI.

```dosbat
C:\>func init demo-function --worker-runtime python --model V2

Writing requirements.txt
Writing function_app.py
Writing .gitignore
Writing host.json
Writing local.settings.json
Writing C:\demo-function\.vscode\extensions.json
```

A basic Azure function project is now created and functional as A `func start` can show. 

```dosbat
C:\demo-function>func start

Azure Functions Core Tools
Core Tools Version:       4.8.0+ec58eb7110992ea02aa19e9c060e45ac8882cc02 (64-bit)
Function Runtime Version: 4.1046.100.25610

[2026-05-21T09:28:04.354Z] No job functions found. Try making your job classes and methods public. If you're using binding extensions (e.g. Azure Storage, ServiceBus, Timers, etc.) make sure you've called the registration method for the extension(s) in your startup code (e.g. builder.AddAzureStorage(), builder.AddServiceBus(), builder.AddTimers(), etc.).
For detailed output, run func with --verbose flag.
```

For now this function is doing nothing so let's iterate on it.

## Adding 1 HTTP triggered function

```dosbat
C:\demo-function>func new --name HttpExample --template "HTTP trigger" --authlevel "function"
The function "HttpExample" was created successfully from the "HTTP trigger" template.
```

The file function_app.py is now updated with a simple function taking one parameter (name) and returning a successful or failure message/code.

Running the function shows an unhealthy state now.

```dosbat
C:\Users\alexa\Documents\PRO_PROJECTS\demo_projects\azure_function_local\demo-function>func start     

Azure Functions Core Tools

```

That unhealthy state points to a storage issue (*azure.functions.webjobs.storage*). Let's install Azurite to simulate a local storage account.



##

Before testing it we need to create a local test environment with appropriate python packages installed `azure-function`

## Creating a local test environment

Let's download and set the Python version of the environment to the latest version of Python 3.14.3 available on pyenv (pyenv install --list) as of today.

```dosbat
C:\>pyenv install 3.14.3
:: [Info] ::  Mirror: https://www.python.org/ftp/python

C:\>pyenv local 3.14.3

C:\>python -m venv .venv
C:\>.venv\Scripts\activate
C:\>python -m pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel
C:\>pip install -r requirements.txt
[...]
Installing collected packages: markupsafe, werkzeug, azure-functions
Successfully installed azure-functions-2.1.0 markupsafe-3.0.3 werkzeug-3.1.8
```

The function now starts successfully.
